subject: Binary format compatibility pin request — provisional fix & checklist
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Binary format compatibility pin request — provisional fix & checklist

Hi all,

Quick summary: Acme AI reported that when they push the Qamar-13B variant (v20271101, model hash: ab12cd34) into our staging fleet the runtime fails during kernel deserialize with a "kv_cache_schema_mismatch" and a handful of OOM traces. They suspect a minor change in the model's binary serialization (endian flag + meta table ordering) compared to the variant we validated last month.

Given customer impact and the fact that this is a compatibility-only regression (no semantic model change), I propose a provisional version pin for the affected hash on the following scope:
- Pin the Qamar-13B ab12cd34 to dedicated ingress in us-west-2 (staging) for 72 hours.
- Run the full compatibility matrix (attached compat_matrix.xlsx) and the lightweight binary-deserializer smoke tests on canary machines.
- If canary passes, allow controlled ingress to additional staging shards; otherwise rollback to last-known-good variant (hash: a9f8e7d6).

Action items I need validated by EOD:
1) Karthik — can infra provision the canary with the provisional pin and run the deserializer smoke-suite (INF-1284)?
2) Soojin — can you confirm tokenizer/kv alignment checks and supply a minimal patch if needed (I attached binary-diff.patch as a stub)?
3) Laura/Marcus — policy approval for a 72-hour provisional pin and telemetry windows (what telemetry thresholds do we treat as auto-rollback?)

Attachments: compat_matrix.xlsx, binary-diff.patch, provisional-escrow-checklist.md

Notes: keeping Acme looped-in to avoid surprises; they are on standby to reproduce if we need additional artifacts.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Product Lead, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Binary format compatibility pin request — provisional fix & checklist

Thanks Priya — I started a canary stack in us-west-2 and triggered the deserializer smoke-suite against ab12cd34. Early results: two failing tests both point to a header-endian mismatch when reading the persisted KV blocks; runtime rejects the precompiled kernels with a "layout signature" mismatch before any heavy compute.

Questions/asks:
- I need the exact serialization spec change from ModelHub or a minimal reproduction. If ModelHub changed the meta table ordering we can either (A) add a small deserializer shim that accepts both orders for 72h, or (B) pin the model and force fallback to a compatible variant. Shim has lower customer friction but needs an emergency kernel path and QA.
- Marcus: can we get temporary elevated logging for the canary (token-level sampling at 10%) so we can detect silent corruptions?

I pushed a WIP PR to the runtime repo with a tolerant deserializer toggle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/742 — this implements option (A) behind a feature flag. If accepted we can flip the flag for canary only.

I recommend provisional pin + toggle on canary while we validate. If shim looks safe in 24h, widen; if not, rollback and require upstream model re-serialization.

- Karthik
Engineering, Serving Runtime
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Binary format compatibility pin request — provisional fix & checklist

Adding details from tokenizer side — I ran a quick compare between the two hashes' tokenizer metadata. The tokenization table itself is identical, but the serialized token index table includes a different integer packing (LE vs BE) in the new artifact. That explains why the kv cache layout looks fine on some hosts and fails on others depending on host endian assumptions.

binary-diff.patch (attached) is a tiny shim that detects both encodings and normalizes to our in-memory format. I also updated the provisional-escrow-checklist.md with extra checks for cross-architecture pulls (x86 vs ARM).

Two caveats:
- The shim will add ~2% CPU overhead during initial ingest; acceptable on canary but should be measured.
- We must ensure canary telemetry for tokenization errors is enabled (INF-1284).

If Karthik's runtime toggle is green on CI, I'm comfortable enabling the shim on canary only and running the full compat_matrix.

— Soojin
Infra/Tokenizer Team
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Binary format compatibility pin request — provisional fix & checklist

All — I approve a 72-hour provisional pin for ab12cd34 on staging with the following guardrails:
- Canary only in us-west-2 for first 24h with feature-flagged tolerant-deserializer (PR#742) and Soojin's shim.
- Telemetry thresholds: any tokenization error rate >0.5% OR memory-error traces >0.1% over 30m window triggers auto-rollback to a9f8e7d6.
- Marcus: enable 10% token-level sampling and verbose canary logs for 48h.
- Priya: coordinate external communication with Acme AI; ask them to postpone broad rollout until we clear the compatibility matrix.

Please update JIRA INF-1284 with final test results and attach logs/compat_matrix.xlsx artifacts. If canary remains green after 48h we can discuss controlled expansion.

Thanks — Laura
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
